selectedBlocks.text: [993] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا خالد عن يونس عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة قال كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ فانكسفت الشمس فقام النبي ﷺ يجر رداءه حتى دخل المسجد فدخلنا فصلى بنا ركعتين حتى انجلت الشمس، فقال ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا وادعوا حتى يكشف ما بكم

[994] حدثنا شهاب بن عباد قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن حميد عن إسماعيل عن قيس قال: سمعت أبا مسعود يقول: قال النبي ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد من الناس ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله فإذا رأيتموهما فقوموا فصلوا

[995] حدثنا أصبغ قال: أخبرني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم حدثه عن أبيه عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه كان يخبر عن النبي ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا

[996] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا هاشم بن القاسم قال: حدثنا شيبان أبو معاوية عن زياد بن علاقة عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال كسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ يوم مات إبراهيم، فقال الناس كسفت الشمس لموت إبراهيم، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم فصلوا وادعوا الله

[997] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أنها قالت خسفت الشمس في عهد رسول الله ﷺ فصلى رسول الله ﷺ بالناس فقام فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم قام فأطال القيام وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع فأطال الركوع وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم سجد فأطال السجود ثم فعل في الركعة الثانية مثل ما فعل في الأولى ثم انصرف وقد انجلت الشمس فخطب الناس فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله لا ينخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك فادعوا الله وكبروا وصلوا وتصدقوا، ثم قال: يا أمة محمد والله ما من أحد أغير من الله أن يزني عبده أو تزني أمته يا أمة محمد والله لو تعلمون ما أعلم لضحكتم قليلا ولبكيتم كثيرا
باب النداء بالصلاة جامعة في الكسوف

[998] حدثني إسحاق قال: أخبرنا يحيى بن صالح قال: حدثنا معاوية بن سلام بن أبي سلام الحبشي الدمشقي قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير قال: أخبرني أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف الزهري عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال لما كسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ نودي إن الصلاة جامعة

segments.arabic: [993] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا خالد عن يونس عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة قال
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ فانكسفت الشمس فقام النبي ﷺ يجر رداءه حتى دخل المسجد فدخلنا فصلى بنا ركعتين حتى انجلت الشمس، فقال ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا وادعوا حتى يكشف ما بكم
segments.english: We were with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up, dragging his cloak, until he entered the mosque. We entered, and he led us in two rak‘ahs until the sun became clear. Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When you see them, pray and supplicate until what has befallen you is removed.”

notes: The selected source has three Prophet honorifics, all retained. Brill opens with the Prophet where the selected source and modern print say the Messenger of Allah. Brill also does not repeat the final honorific; the modern print agrees with the selected text.

The Bewley comparison adds a house location that is not explicit in this selected Arabic. The working English does not import that location. The closing expression retains what has befallen you rather than replacing it with an inferred explanation.

segments.arabic: [994] حدثنا شهاب بن عباد قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن حميد عن إسماعيل عن قيس قال: سمعت أبا مسعود يقول:
segments.english: Shihab ibn ‘Abbad related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Humayd related to us, from Isma‘il, from Qays, who said: I heard Abu Mas‘ud saying:

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد من الناس ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله فإذا رأيتموهما فقوموا فصلوا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of the death of any person. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, stand up and pray.”

notes: The full chain retains Qays saying I heard Abu Masud. The selected instruction to stand is kept, as is the reference to a person among the people.
This occurrence is not merged with 1008, whose selected wording and narrator chain differ.

segments.arabic: [995] حدثنا أصبغ قال: أخبرني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم حدثه عن أبيه عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه كان يخبر عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Asbagh related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me. He said: ‘Amr informed me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who related it to him, from his father, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who used to report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: إن الشمس والقمر لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا
segments.english: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, pray.”

notes: The selected relative clause that Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related it to him is retained; no narrator name is silently added to its pronoun. Brill omits this relative clause, while the modern print retains it. Both singular informed-me verbs remain distinct.
The selected companion honorific includes Most High and both persons. Brill lacks this companion honorific; the modern print has the shorter form without Most High.
Life remains life; the birth gloss in the Khan comparison is not inserted. The full attribution to the Prophet remains in the expandable chain and complete narration script.

segments.arabic: [996] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا هاشم بن القاسم قال: حدثنا شيبان أبو معاوية عن زياد بن علاقة عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us. He said: Shayban Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

segments.arabic: كسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ يوم مات إبراهيم، فقال الناس كسفت الشمس لموت إبراهيم، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم فصلوا وادعوا الله
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the day Ibrahim died. The people said: “The sun was eclipsed because of Ibrahim’s death.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see this, pray and supplicate to Allah.”

notes: The selected source names Ibrahim without adding son or a historical date. The two Messenger honorifics remain complete.

The Bewley comparison includes a signs clause absent from this occurrence in the selected source and inspected prints. Brill adds a final divine epithet not present in the selected wording. Neither is imported.
When you see this supplies the understood object of the Arabic verb in English. It does not add a new event or change the following prayer and supplication instructions.

segments.arabic: [997] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘Aishah, who said:

segments.arabic: خسفت الشمس في عهد رسول الله ﷺ فصلى رسول الله ﷺ بالناس فقام فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم قام فأطال القيام وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع فأطال الركوع وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم سجد فأطال السجود ثم فعل في الركعة الثانية مثل ما فعل في الأولى ثم انصرف وقد انجلت الشمس فخطب الناس فحمد الله وأثنى عليه،
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led the people in prayer. He stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, but it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, but it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he did in the second rak‘ah as he had done in the first. Then he finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him.

segments.arabic: ثم قال إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله لا ينخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك فادعوا الله وكبروا وصلوا وتصدقوا،
segments.english: Then he said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see this, supplicate to Allah, proclaim His greatness, pray and give charity.”

segments.arabic: ثم قال: يا أمة محمد والله ما من أحد أغير من الله أن يزني عبده أو تزني أمته يا أمة محمد والله لو تعلمون ما أعلم لضحكتم قليلا ولبكيتم كثيرا
segments.english: Then he said: “O community of Muhammad, by Allah, no one has greater ghayrah than Allah concerning His male servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse or His female servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse. O community of Muhammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.”

checkedBody: In the life-time of Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) the sun eclipsed, so he led the people in prayer, and stood up and performed a long Qiyam, then bowed for a long while. He stood up again and performed a long Qiyam but this time the period of standing was shorter than the first. He bowed again for a long time but shorter than the first one, then he prostrated and prolonged the prostration. He did the same in the second Raka as he did in the first and then finished the prayer; by then the sun (eclipse) had cleared. He delivered the Khutba (sermon) and after praising and glorifying Allah he said, "The sun and the moon are two signs against the signs of Allah; they do not eclipse on the death or life of anyone. So when you see the eclipse, remember Allah and say Takbir, pray and give Sadaqa." The Prophet then said, "O followers of Muhammad! By Allah! There is none who has more ghaira (self-respect) than Allah as He has forbidden that His slaves, male or female commit adultery (illegal sexual intercourse). O followers of Muhammad! By Allah! If you knew that which I know you would laugh little and weep much.
comparisons.damagedExcerpt: two signs against the signs of Allah
comparisons.note: The pinned body contains a damaged preposition in the signs clause and explanatory renderings in the supplication and ghayrah clauses. It locates this report but cannot supply pristine wording for the complete selected Arabic or chain.

notes: The selected description retains both standings and bowings before the first prostration, and the statement that the second rakah followed the first. Both closing addresses and both oaths are preserved. No additional prayer formula or recitation is supplied from another occurrence.

The pinned Khan body has against in the signs clause. It also paraphrases the selected supplicate instruction as remember and adds an explanatory prohibition in the ghayrah clause. Those features are not copied into the working English.

Ghayrah is deliberately retained as a transliterated term in this provisional English. Bewley uses jealous; Khan retains ghaira with a self-respect gloss. Ibn Hajar discusses the term and different explanatory approaches. No explanatory theological paraphrase is inserted into the hadith. Independent lexical and theological review remains pending.

Unlawful sexual intercourse preserves the scope of zina without limiting it to married persons. Servant retains each of the male and female forms in the selected wording. Proclaim His greatness renders the takbir instruction without importing a separate formula.

Brill includes an Aishah honorific not present in this selected paragraph or the modern print. Brill names the second unit as the other unit. The selected text and its exact honorific coverage are preserved unchanged.

segments.arabic: [998] حدثني إسحاق قال: أخبرنا يحيى بن صالح قال: حدثنا معاوية بن سلام بن أبي سلام الحبشي الدمشقي قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير قال: أخبرني أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف الزهري عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Ishaq related to me. He said: Yahya ibn Salih informed us. He said: Mu‘awiyah ibn Sallam ibn Abi Sallam al-Habashi al-Dimashqi related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us. He said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf al-Zuhri informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: لما كسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ نودي إن الصلاة جامعة
segments.english: When the sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the announcement was made: “The prayer is in congregation.”

notes: The entire long narrator chain is retained, including the Habashi, Dimashqi and Zuhri affiliations and the companion honorific with Most High and both persons.

The selected Ishaq verb is related to me; both inspected prints have related to us. Brill also has singular verbs for Muawiyah and Yahya where the selected source and modern print have plural verbs. These source-specific differences are exposed rather than silently normalized or declared to be transcription errors.
The prayer is in congregation renders the quoted announcement. The caller is not identified, and no ordinary adhan wording is added.
